gold: Acute dacryocystitis with secondary optic nerve injury
e7_s4_rationale: The presence of a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding and globe compression due to increased abscess size, along with a history of epiphora, strongly supports this diagnosis. The isolation of Streptococcus pyogenes further confirms an infectious process.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Orbital cellulitis
e7_s4_rejected.why: While there is inflammation, the specific finding of a lacrimal sac abscess points more directly to this condition.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
e7_s4_rejected.why: The presence of a specific infectious agent (Streptococcus pyogenes) and a lacrimal sac abscess makes this less likely.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
e7_s4_rejected.why: There is no mention of symptoms or findings suggestive of cavernous sinus involvement, such as bilateral eye findings or specific neurologic deficits.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Orbital apex syndrome
e7_s4_rejected.why: This condition typically involves multiple cranial nerves and has more severe and complex presentations, which are not fully aligned with the provided case facts.
